result.reason: The operative language gives Corio a 30-day convenience-termination right and a refund of prepaid fees attributable to the post-termination period, while denying Commerce One a convenience right, so it substantively reaches the preferred position. However, allowing termination “in whole or in part” exceeds the playbook and may disrupt scope, pricing, and other commercial arrangements without addressing the consequences of partial termination. The unqualified statement that Commerce One has no convenience-termination right may also conflict with or eliminate its existing end-of-term nonrenewal right, whereas the preferred position only prohibits vendor termination during a committed term. The clause should be limited to whole-agreement termination and clarify that Commerce One may still elect not to renew as permitted by Section 11.1.
